candidates.api_shape: hart_inversor(long_len, short_len, crank_angle_deg) -> {bars..., tracer, joints} plus hart_pose(...) returning the inversor points and the line
candidates.fdm: Flat bars stacked like peaucellier_linkage. No slideway. Pose is one crank or cell angle; tracer Q is exact on a line. W-frame first (6 bars); A-frame is a variant, not a second API.
candidates.name: hart_inversor
candidates.why: Exact planar straight line with six bars and only revolute joints. The name people look up after Peaucellier. Used in instruments and as a compact inversor cell. Hart's first form is the W-frame (antiparallelogram); the A-frame is the second.

candidates.api_shape: tusi_couple(ring_teeth, module, pin_phase_deg) -> {ring, planet, pin} plus tusi_pose(phase_deg) -> pin on a diameter
candidates.fdm: ring_gear plus a half-tooth planet, pin on the pitch circle, optional slider that the pin drives. Print gears flat. Pose: planet spin = -2 * orbit; pin (x,y) collapses to a diameter.
candidates.name: tusi_couple
candidates.why: Exact straight diameter from a planet rolling inside a ring of twice the pitch. Cardanic motion; Murray hypocycloidal engines; any point on the planet pitch circle reciprocates on a diameter. Distinct from ring_gear_mesh (ratio drive) and from scotch_yoke (slot inversion of the same law).

candidates.already: four_bar (lengths only; no T, no error)
candidates.api_shape: hoecken_pose(unit, crank_angle_deg) -> {O1,O2,A,B,T}; hoecken_linkage(...) -> kit plus max_error and velocity_ratio
candidates.fdm: Same stacked-bar kit as four_bar, with coupler_ext as a first-class tracer and a max_error like chebyshev_linkage. Prints flat.
candidates.name: hoecken_linkage
candidates.why: The approximate 4-bar whose coupler point holds a long, nearly constant-velocity straight line. Walking feet, pick-and-place, film transports. four_bar defaults are Hoecken lengths but four_bar_pose does not return the tracer or measure path error.

candidates.api_shape: trammel(a, b, bar_len, phase_deg) -> {rail_x, rail_y, slider_x, slider_y, bar} plus trammel_pose -> ellipse point
candidates.fdm: Two short linear ways at 90 degrees plus a bar with two sliding pins. oldham_coupling and scotch_yoke are inversions, not this generator. Pose is one crank or slider coordinate.
candidates.name: trammel
candidates.why: Archimedes ellipsograph / double-slider: two prismatic joints on perpendicular axes, a rod through both sliders. Any point on the rod traces an ellipse; the sliders themselves are the straight constraints. Used as an ellipse generator and as the Baker-Cross / inverted-Oldham engine core.

candidates.already: four_bar (can be dialed in if you know the lengths and coupler point)
candidates.api_shape: roberts_pose(unit, crank_angle_deg) -> {O1,O2,A,B,T}; roberts_linkage(...) kit plus max_error
candidates.fdm: Same as four_bar plus a named tracer. Worth a pose helper so agents do not invent proportions.
candidates.name: roberts_linkage
candidates.why: Named isosceles 4-bar whose coupler point traces a long approximate straight line (different curve from Watt and Chebyshev). Teaching set and one of the five UC Davis four-bar straight-line examples.

candidates.api_shape: evans_pose(unit, crank_angle_deg) -> joints plus T, or leave as a four_bar recipe
candidates.fdm: Prints as bars. Low leverage next to Hoecken and Roberts, which cover the same job with better-known proportions.
candidates.name: evans_grasshopper
candidates.why: Evans 1801 approximate straight-line, the grasshopper beam-engine motion. Historical more than reused. A 4-bar with a long coupler extension.

rejected.name: sarrus_linkage
rejected.why: Already sarrus_pose + sarrus_linkage. Exact spatial straight line.

rejected.name: scott_russell_linkage
rejected.why: Already scott_russell_pose + scott_russell_linkage. Exact, spends one P pair.

rejected.name: watt_linkage
rejected.why: Already watt_pose + watt_linkage with measured error.

rejected.name: chebyshev_linkage
rejected.why: Already chebyshev_pose + chebyshev_linkage (lambda form). The non-lambda Chebyshev is a cognate; do not ship both kits.

rejected.name: watt_parallel_motion
rejected.why: Compound of Watt plus a pantograph. Both parts exist. A glued product, not a new primitive.

rejected.name: scotch_yoke_as_straight_line
rejected.why: Already scotch_yoke. It is a Tusi inversion used as a yoke, not a missing generator.

rejected.name: oldham_as_trammel
rejected.why: Already oldham_coupling. Same Cardanic family, different job (misaligned shafts).

rejected.name: kempe_bricard_perrolatz_quadruplanar
rejected.why: Exact inversors with more bars or unstable positions. Hart is the one 6-bar to add first. The rest are gallery trivia.

rejected.name: horse_head_jib
rejected.why: Level-luffing crane product, not a pair/kit.

rejected.name: multifaze_stiller_smith
rejected.why: Finished engine using trammel/Tusi. Out of scope.

rejected.name: flexure_stage
rejected.why: Already the compliant straight line. Not missing.

sources: Kempe, A.B. How to Draw a Straight Line, Macmillan 1877
summary: A straight-line mechanism turns rotation or rocking into a stroke of definite length. Four-bars can only approximate a line (Watt 1784); exact planar lines need either a prismatic pair or an inversor cell that inverts a circle through a point into a line. Mechlib already covers the main teaching set with pose APIs: peaucellier_pose/linkage (exact 7-bar inversor), sarrus_pose/linkage (exact spatial, first perfect line, 1853), scott_russell_pose/linkage (exact half-length inversor that spends one P pair), watt_pose/linkage (approximate, error measured), and chebyshev_pose/linkage (lambda, 4:5:2, error measured). four_bar defaults claim Hoecken proportions and mention the coupler passing under O1, but four_bar_pose returns only O1/O2/A/B: no tracer T, no path-error metric, no named hoecken_* API. scotch_yoke and oldham_coupling are Tusi/Cardanic inversions used as a yoke and a coupling, not as a straight-line generator. flexure_stage is the compliant straight line. Missing exact generators that still earn a kit: Hart's W-frame (6-bar inversor, two bars fewer than Peaucellier, the next name after Peaucellier in every textbook) and a Tusi couple (internal ring of twice the planet pitch, a point on the planet pitch circle traces a diameter). Missing named approximate kits: Hoecken (constant-velocity walking/pick-and-place line), Roberts (isosceles 4-bar), and Evans grasshopper. Trammel of Archimedes is an ellipsograph / double-slider; it shares kinematics with Oldham and Scotch yoke but is not those products. Rejected as already covered: a second Peaucellier, Watt, Chebyshev lambda, Scott-Russell, or Sarrus. Rejected as teaching-only extras: Kempe kites, Bricard, Perrolatz, Sylvester-Kempe and Kumara-Kampling quadruplanar inversors (Hart first). Rejected as products: horse-head crane jibs, Chebyshev tables, MultiFAZE/Stiller-Smith engines, Watt parallel-motion as a compound Watt+pantograph product (both parts already exist).
title: Straight-line and inversor linkages
